formables.title: the Nordic Union
formables.desc: Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland have shared kings, wars and a common heritage for centuries. United, the North would be a power no empire could ignore.

formables.title: the Iberian Union
formables.desc: Twice before the crowns of Castile, Aragon and Portugal have been joined. A single Iberian state would command the gateway between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

formables.title: the United Netherlands

names.totalist: People's Republic of the Low Countries
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Republic of the Low Countries
names.market_liberal: United Provinces of the Low Countries

formables.desc: The Low Countries were one realm before the revolution of 1830 tore them apart. Reuniting Holland, Flanders, Wallonia and Luxembourg would restore the old Burgundian inheritance.

formables.title: the Danubian Federation
formables.desc: Kossuth proposed a Danubian Confederation of Hungarians, Romanians, Serbs and Croats. Add the Austrian and Czech lands and the peoples of the Danube basin could build what the Habsburgs never did.

formables.title: Yugoslavia

names.social_conservative: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

formables.desc: The South Slavs share a language and a long history of foreign rule. Belgrade, Zagreb and Ljubljana under one roof would form the strongest power in the Balkans.

formables.title: the Balkan Federation
formables.desc: For a century the Balkans have been the powder keg of Europe, their small states played against each other by the great powers. Only a federation of all Balkan peoples can end that game.

formables.title: the Baltic Federation
formables.desc: Squeezed between Germany and Russia, the Baltic peoples can only secure their future together.

formables.title: the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
formables.desc: The Commonwealth of the Two Nations once stretched from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Its partition was a crime; its restoration is a duty.

formables.title: the Holy Roman Empire

names.paternal_autocrat: Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation

formables.desc: Charlemagne's crown passed to the German kings and was laid down in 1806. Whoever holds Berlin, Vienna, Prague, Aachen, Munich and Milan may take it up again.

formables.title: Francia
formables.desc: Long before France and Germany, there was the realm of the Franks. Restore the borders of Charlemagne and the old quarrel along the Rhine ends forever.

formables.title: the Roman Empire
formables.desc: All roads lead to Rome. From the Pillars of Hercules to the walls of Jerusalem, the Mediterranean will once again be Mare Nostrum.

formables.title: the Byzantine Empire
formables.desc: Constantinople fell in 1453, but the Great Idea never died. With the City and Anatolia in Greek hands, the Empire of the Romans can rise again.

formables.title: the Greater Maghreb
formables.desc: From the Atlantic coast of Morocco to the shores of Libya, the Maghreb shares one faith, one history and one destiny.

formables.title: the Arab Federation
formables.desc: The Arab Revolt promised a single Arab nation from the Taurus to Yemen. That promise can still be kept.

formables.title: the Nile Valley Union

names.totalist: People's Republic of the Nile Valley
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Republic of the Nile Valley
names.social_conservative: Kingdom of Egypt and the Sudan
names.authoritarian_democrat: Kingdom of Egypt and the Sudan
names.paternal_autocrat: Sultanate of Egypt and the Sudan

formables.desc: The Nile is one river, and its valley should be one country, from Alexandria to Khartoum and the lakes of Equatoria where the Khedives once flew their flag.

formables.title: the Transcaucasian Federation
formables.desc: The Transcaucasian Federation of 1918 lasted barely a month. With Tiflis, Erivan and Baku united, the mountain peoples can try again and stand against Russia and Turkey alike.

formables.title: Greater Iran
formables.desc: The lands of the Shahnameh stretch from the Caucasus to the Hindu Kush. A new Iranian empire would restore the reach of the Safavids.

formables.title: Turan
formables.desc: From the Caspian to the Tarim basin, the Turkic peoples of Central Asia have been ruled by Tsars and Chinese warlords for too long. United, they can be masters of their own steppe.

formables.title: the Mongol Empire
formables.desc: Seven centuries ago the descendants of Chinggis Khan ruled half the world. The Mongols of Urga, Inner Mongolia, Buryatia and Dzungaria can at least rule themselves together.

formables.title: the West African Federation
formables.desc: The colonial borders of West Africa were drawn by Europeans in Berlin. A federation from Dakar to Lagos would erase them.

formables.title: the East African Federation
formables.desc: The Great Lakes and the Swahili coast are one region, joined by trade for a thousand years. United, East Africa can finally govern itself.

formables.title: the Central African Federation
formables.desc: Rhodesia, Barotseland and Nyasaland share the Zambezi and its railways. Joined together, they would form a strong state in the heart of southern Africa.

formables.title: Greater Ethiopia

names.syndicalist: Union of Communes of the Horn
names.social_liberal: Federation of the Horn of Africa

formables.desc: Ethiopia alone in Africa never bowed to a colonial master. Its rule over Eritrea, Somalia and the coast would make the Horn of Africa one power.

formables.title: the United Congo
formables.desc: King Leopold's Congo was divided by its warlords and companies. Whoever reunites the river basin will hold the richest land in Africa.

formables.title: the United States of Africa
formables.desc: Pan-Africanists have long dreamed of a single African nation, free of every colonial master. Hold the great capitals of the continent and make that dream real.

formables.title: Maphilindo
formables.desc: The Malay peoples of the Philippines, Malaya and the Indies are one nation divided by colonial empires. Maphilindo would unite them in a single archipelagic state.

formables.title: Gran Colombia
formables.desc: Bolívar's republic broke apart in 1831. Bogotá, Caracas, Quito and Panama together would restore the Liberator's dream.

formables.title: the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
formables.desc: Santa Cruz's confederation of Peru and Bolivia was destroyed by its jealous neighbours in 1839. Its time has come again.

formables.title: Tawantinsuyu
formables.desc: The four quarters of the Inca world ran from Quito to the Maule river. Restoring Tawantinsuyu would honour the Andean peoples who have endured four centuries of foreign rule.

formables.title: the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

names.base: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Republic of the Río de la Plata
names.social_democrat: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.social_liberal: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.social_conservative: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.authoritarian_democrat: Confederation of the Río de la Plata
names.paternal_autocrat: Kingdom of the Río de la Plata

formables.desc: Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Asunción were once capitals of a single viceroyalty. The River Plate should have one master.

formables.title: the Union of South American Nations

names.totalist: Union of South American Socialist Republics

formables.desc: From the Caribbean to Cape Horn, South America shares a common struggle for independence. Hold its six great capitals and the continent will speak with one voice.

formables.title: the North American Union

names.totalist: Union of North American Socialist Republics

formables.desc: Washington, Ottawa and Mexico City under one government would create the most powerful state the world has ever seen.

formables.title: the Pan-Slavic Union
formables.desc: The Slavic Congress of 1848 dreamed of brotherhood between all Slavic peoples. Moscow, Kyiv, Warsaw, Prague, Belgrade and Sofia united would dominate Eastern Europe.

formables.title: the European Federation
formables.desc: Napoleon tried and failed; the Kaiser came close. Paris, Berlin, London, Rome, Madrid, Vienna and Warsaw in one hand would finally make Europe a single nation.

formables.title: Greater Germany
formables.desc: All Germans in one state, from the North Sea to the Alps and from Alsace to the Sudetenland: the old pan-German dream.

formables.title: the Greater German Solution
formables.desc: The Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 wanted a German nation that included the Austrian lands, Bohemia and Trieste. Bismarck chose the smaller solution; the larger one is still possible.

formables.title: Germany
formables.desc: With the old Empire broken, each of its successor states claims to be the true Germany. Only one of them can reunite it.

formables.title: the South German Federation
formables.desc: Bavaria, Württemberg, Baden and Hesse were sovereign kingdoms and grand duchies within living memory. Together they could stand apart from Prussia.

formables.title: the North German Confederation
formables.desc: In 1867 Prussia gathered the northern German states into a confederation under its leadership. Restore it, under whatever flag now flies over Berlin.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Prussia
formables.desc: Frederick the Great's kingdom was the iron core of Germany. Let it stand on its own again, from the Rhine to the Memel.

formables.title: the Teutonic Order

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Prussia and Livonia

formables.desc: For three centuries the Knights ruled the Baltic shore from Danzig to Reval. A new Grand Master can take up their mantle.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Livonia
formables.desc: Ivan the Terrible once crowned a vassal King of Livonia. The Baltic barons, Latvians and Estonians could build a real one.

formables.title: the Hanseatic League
formables.desc: The merchant cities of the Hansa once dominated trade from London to Novgorod. Bind the Baltic ports together again.

formables.title: D-A-CH
formables.desc: Germany, Austria and Switzerland share a language and an economy. Why not a single federation?

formables.title: the Alpine Federation
formables.desc: The cantons, Tyrol and the Bavarian highlands share mountain passes, dialects and a stubborn love of self-rule.

formables.title: Austria-Hungary
formables.desc: The Dual Monarchy is coming apart at the seams. Hold it together, or forge it anew, from Bohemia to Transylvania.

formables.title: the United States of Greater Austria
formables.desc: Aurel Popovici's plan of 1906 would have rebuilt the Habsburg realm as fifteen national states under one emperor. It has never been tried.

formables.title: the Austro-Slovak Union
formables.desc: Pressburg lies forty miles from Vienna. A union of Austria and Slovakia would join two halves of the same valley.

formables.title: the Lands of the Bohemian Crown
formables.desc: Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia were crowned together for four centuries. Restore the Crown of Saint Wenceslas.

formables.title: Great Moravia

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Moravia and Slovakia

formables.desc: Before Bohemia and Hungary, Great Moravia was the first Slavic state of Central Europe. Svätopluk's realm can rise again.

formables.title: the Visegrad Union
formables.desc: In 1335 the kings of Poland, Bohemia and Hungary met at Visegrad to make common cause. Their heirs can finish the job.

formables.title: Zapadoslavia
formables.desc: Poles, Czechs, Slovaks and Sorbs are the western branch of the Slavic family. Zapadoslavia would gather them into one state.

formables.title: Intermarium
formables.desc: Piłsudski dreamed of a federation between the Baltic, Black and Adriatic seas, strong enough to stand between Germany and Russia.

formables.title: the Polish-Hungarian Union
formables.desc: "Pole and Hungarian, two good brothers." The two nations shared kings in the fourteenth century and a friendship ever since.

formables.title: the Polish-Romanian Union
formables.desc: Poland and Romania share a border and a fear of the same neighbours. A union would turn that common cause into a single state.

formables.title: the Polish-Swedish Union
formables.desc: Sigismund Vasa wore both the Polish and the Swedish crowns. His dream of a Baltic union under one king can be revived.

formables.title: the Grand Duchy of Lithuania
formables.desc: Medieval Lithuania ruled from the Baltic to the Black Sea. A new Grand Duke can gather the lands of the Rus' that once looked to Vilnius.

formables.title: Kievan Rus'
formables.desc: A thousand years ago Kiev was the mother of the cities of the Rus'. Whoever holds Kiev and Novgorod can claim Yaroslav the Wise's inheritance.

formables.title: the Russian Empire
formables.desc: The Romanov empire stretched from the Vistula to the Pacific. Its heirs are fighting over its corpse; the victor may resurrect it.

formables.title: the Cossack Hosts

names.social_liberal: Federal Republic of the Cossack Lands

formables.desc: From the Don to the Amur, the Cossack hosts guarded the frontiers of the Tsars for centuries. Bound together, they would answer to no one.

formables.title: the Crimean Khanate
formables.desc: For three centuries the Giray khans ruled Crimea and the steppe to its north. The Crimean Tatars can restore their state.

formables.title: the Golden Horde
formables.desc: Batu Khan's horde ruled the steppe from the Danube to Siberia and took tribute from Moscow. The Tatars of the Volga can raise its banner again.

formables.title: the Avar Khaganate
formables.desc: Before the Magyars came, the Avar khagans ruled the Pannonian plain for two hundred years and besieged Constantinople.

formables.title: the Hunnic Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Carpatho-Pontic Lands

formables.desc: Attila's empire stretched from the Rhine to the Volga and made Rome pay tribute. A new Scourge of God could rise on the Hungarian plain.

formables.title: the Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen

names.base: Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen
names.social_conservative: Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen

formables.desc: Hungarians will not forgive the dismemberment of their kingdom. Restore the Crown of Saint Stephen from the Adriatic to the Carpathians.

formables.title: Carpathia
formables.desc: The Rusyns, Hutsuls and Lemkos of the mountains have always been ruled from distant capitals. A Carpathian state would be their own.

formables.title: Dacia
formables.desc: Burebista and Decebalus ruled the Dacians from the Carpathians before Rome came. Unite every Romanian land under the old name.

formables.title: the Bulgarian-Romanian Union
formables.desc: The Danube divides Bulgaria and Romania, but the two Orthodox kingdoms have more in common with each other than with any other neighbour.

formables.title: the Bulgarian Empire
formables.desc: Under Tsar Simeon the Great, Bulgaria ruled the Balkans between three seas. Restore the First Bulgarian Empire.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Thrace
formables.desc: Before Macedon, the Odrysian kings ruled Thrace from the Danube to the Aegean. The land between Sofia and Constantinople can be one country again.

formables.title: the Illyrian Kingdom
formables.desc: Queen Teuta's Illyrians held the eastern Adriatic before Rome. Albanians, Montenegrins and Dalmatians all claim descent from them.

formables.title: Greater Albania
formables.desc: Half the Albanian nation lives outside Albania. Bring Kosovo, Chameria and western Macedonia home.

formables.title: Greater Serbia
formables.desc: Wherever a Serb lives, there is Serbia, say the nationalists. From Banja Luka to Skopje, make it so.

formables.title: Greater Croatia
formables.desc: The kingdom of Tomislav reached from the Drava to the Adriatic. Greater Croatia would add Međimurje and the Croats of Bačka to Bosnia and Dalmatia.

formables.title: Greater Yugoslavia
formables.desc: South Slav visionaries have long imagined Yugoslavia and Bulgaria as one state, with Albania to follow. Build the greatest power in the Balkans.

formables.title: the Adriatic Union
formables.desc: The Adriatic has been a Venetian lake and an Austrian one. A federation of all its shores would end the quarrel between Italians and South Slavs.

formables.title: Greater Greece

names.social_conservative: Greece of Two Continents and Five Seas

formables.desc: The Megali Idea: a Greece of two continents and five seas, with Constantinople as its capital. Every Greek government has dreamed of it.

formables.title: the Greco-Turkish Union
formables.desc: Greeks and Turks have shared the Aegean for a thousand years, more often as enemies than friends. Some have dreamed of one state for both peoples.

formables.title: the Macedonian Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Hellenistic World

formables.desc: Alexander marched from Pella to the Indus in eleven years. His successors divided the world he conquered. Put it back together.

formables.title: the Seleucid Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Syria and Mesopotamia

formables.desc: Seleucus, one of Alexander's generals, built an empire from Antioch to Persia. Syria and Mesopotamia shared a Hellenistic crown for two centuries.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Pontus
formables.desc: Mithridates of Pontus fought Rome for forty years from his Black Sea capital. The Pontic Greeks have asked for a republic of their own.

formables.title: the United British Isles

names.totalist: People's Republic of the British Isles
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Federation of the British Isles
names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the British Isles
names.social_conservative: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
names.authoritarian_democrat: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
names.paternal_autocrat: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

formables.desc: Ireland broke away and the Union of Britain drove the King into exile. Reunite all four nations of the isles under one government.

formables.title: the Celtic Union
formables.desc: Irish, Scots, Welsh, Bretons, Cornish, Manx and Galicians: seven Celtic nations on the Atlantic edge of Europe. Unite them all.

formables.title: the Angevin Empire
formables.desc: Henry II ruled England, Normandy, Anjou and Aquitaine, more of France than the French king. Rebuild the Angevin realm on both sides of the Channel.

formables.title: the North Sea Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the North Sea

formables.desc: Cnut the Great was king of England, Denmark and Norway at once. The North Sea was his lake.

formables.title: Denmark-Norway

names.social_conservative: United Kingdoms of Denmark and Norway

formables.desc: For four centuries Norway was ruled from Copenhagen under the Dannebrog. Bring the twin kingdoms back together.

formables.title: Sweden-Norway

names.social_conservative: United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway

formables.desc: From 1814 to 1905 Sweden and Norway shared one king. The union could be revived on equal terms.

formables.title: the Swedish Empire
formables.desc: In the seventeenth century the Baltic was a Swedish lake, from Finland and Livonia to Pomerania. Gustavus Adolphus would want it back.

formables.title: Greater Norway
formables.desc: Norway once ruled Iceland, Greenland, the Faroes and the Scottish isles. Norse romantics call the old realm Greater Norway.

formables.title: Greater Finland
formables.desc: Finnish nationalists dream of a Greater Finland reaching to the White Sea and the Gulf of Finland, home to every Finnic people.

formables.title: Fennoscandia
formables.desc: Geologists call it Fennoscandia: Scandinavia, Finland, Karelia and the Kola peninsula, one ancient shield of rock. Make it one country.

formables.title: the Great Nordic Union

names.social_liberal: Federal Republic of the Greater North
names.authoritarian_democrat: Federal State of the Greater North

formables.desc: The Nordic countries and the Baltic states share a sea and centuries of Viking, Hanseatic and Swedish history. A Great Nordic Union would make the Baltic a Nordic lake.

formables.title: the French Empire
formables.desc: At its height in 1812 Napoleon's Empire stretched from Hamburg to Rome and from Amsterdam to Dubrovnik. Vive l'Empereur!

formables.title: the Franco-Spanish Union
formables.desc: "There are no more Pyrenees," Louis XIV is said to have declared when his grandson took the Spanish throne. Make it true.

formables.title: the Gallic Empire
formables.desc: In 260 the general Postumus broke away from Rome and ruled Gaul, Britain and Spain as emperor for fourteen years.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Burgundy
formables.desc: Charles the Bold ruled Burgundy and the Low Countries and wanted a crown to match. He died at Nancy before he got it.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Lotharingia
formables.desc: When Charlemagne's empire was split in 843, Lothair got the middle, from Frisia through the Rhineland to Italy. The lands between France and Germany could be a nation.

formables.title: the Crown of Aragon
formables.desc: The Crown of Aragon ruled the western Mediterranean from Barcelona: Valencia, Majorca, Sardinia, Sicily and Naples.

formables.title: Al-Andalus
formables.desc: For seven centuries Muslim al-Andalus was among the most advanced societies in Europe, with Córdoba as its jewel.

formables.title: the Visigothic Kingdom
formables.desc: The Visigoths ruled Hispania and Septimania from Toledo until 711. Spanish monarchists trace their nation back to them.

formables.title: the Ostrogothic Kingdom
formables.desc: Theodoric the Great ruled Italy from Ravenna as Gothic king and Roman governor at once, and kept the peace for thirty years.

formables.title: the Vandal Kingdom
formables.desc: The Vandals crossed from Spain to Africa, took Carthage, and in 455 sacked Rome itself. Their kingdom ruled the islands of the western Mediterranean.

formables.title: the Romano-Gothic Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Gothic West

formables.desc: The Gothic king Ataulf once dreamed of replacing Romania with Gothia. Unite the Visigothic and Ostrogothic realms into one empire of Goths and Romans.

formables.title: the Western Roman Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Western Mediterranean

formables.desc: Rome fell in the West in 476 but lasted another thousand years in the East. Restore the Western Empire from Britannia to Africa.

formables.title: the Latin Union

names.social_liberal: Federal Republic of the Latin Nations

formables.desc: French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italians and Romanians all speak daughters of Latin. A Latin Union would rival the Germanic and Slavic worlds.

formables.title: Italy
formables.desc: Italy has been torn apart by war and revolution. Whoever reunites the peninsula will finish the work of Garibaldi.

formables.title: Greater Italy
formables.desc: Italia irredenta: Nice, Corsica, Ticino, Dalmatia and Malta, every land where Italian is spoken. The irredentists will not rest until all of it is Italian.

formables.title: the German Colonial Empire

names.syndicalist: Union of German and Overseas Communes

formables.desc: Most German colonies are governed through puppet administrations. Bring them under direct rule from Berlin and proclaim a true colonial empire.

formables.title: the Dutch Colonial Empire

names.syndicalist: Union of Dutch and Overseas Communes

formables.desc: The Dutch Republic built a trading empire from the Cape to the Spice Islands. The Netherlands can rebuild it as one realm.

formables.title: the Danish Colonial Empire

names.syndicalist: Union of Danish and Overseas Communes

formables.desc: Denmark once held the Virgin Islands, the Gold Coast forts, Tranquebar and the Nicobars as well as Iceland and Greenland. Rebuild the old realm.

formables.title: the Portuguese Empire

names.syndicalist: Union of Portuguese and Overseas Communes
names.social_conservative: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves

formables.desc: Portugal built the first global empire, from Brazil to Macau. Lisbon can make it whole again.

formables.title: the Spanish Empire

names.syndicalist: Union of Spanish and Overseas Communes

formables.desc: The empire on which the sun never set, from Madrid to Mexico, Lima, Buenos Aires and Manila. Spain can claim it all again.

formables.title: the Ottoman Empire
formables.desc: The Sick Man of Europe is not dead yet. Restore the Sultan's authority from the Balkans to Baghdad and Mecca.

formables.title: the Great Ottoman Empire

names.totalist: Union of Near Eastern Socialist Republics
names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Ottoman World

formables.desc: Under Suleiman the Magnificent the Empire besieged Vienna and ruled three continents. Reach that height again.

formables.title: Misak-ı Milli Turkey
formables.desc: Turkish nationalists drew the line of the National Pact: Anatolia, Mosul, Aleppo, Batumi and Western Thrace. Hold every inch of it.

formables.title: Greater Armenia
formables.desc: Armenian nationalists claim the six vilayets of eastern Anatolia, Karabakh and Cilicia. Take everything on their map.

formables.title: Greater Azerbaijan
formables.desc: The Azerbaijani nation lives on both banks of the Aras, divided between Russia and Persia since 1828. Tabriz and Baku belong together.

formables.title: Greater Georgia
formables.desc: Queen Tamar ruled from the Black Sea to the Caspian. Georgia can reclaim Abkhazia, Lazistan and Saingilo.

formables.title: the Qara Qoyunlu

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Eastern Anatolia and Azerbaijan

formables.desc: The Black Sheep Turkomans ruled from Tabriz to Baghdad in the fifteenth century. The Turkic peoples of Azerbaijan and eastern Anatolia can unite again.

formables.title: the Aq Qoyunlu

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Turkoman Lands

formables.desc: The White Sheep Turkomans of Uzun Hasan ruled from Diyarbakir to Isfahan. Their confederation could be rebuilt.

formables.title: the Seljuk Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Iran and Anatolia

formables.desc: Tughril Beg carried Turkic power from Merv to Baghdad and his heirs took Anatolia. Rebuild the Great Seljuk Empire.

formables.title: the Sasanian Empire
formables.desc: For four centuries the Sasanian shahanshahs stood as equals to Rome. Restore Ērānšahr from Ctesiphon to Merv.

formables.title: the Afsharid Empire
formables.desc: Nader Shah drove out the Afghans, humbled the Ottomans and sacked Delhi. His empire died with him; it need not stay dead.

formables.title: the Qajar Empire
formables.desc: Before the treaty of Turkmenchay the Qajar shahs ruled Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan. Win back what Russia took.

formables.title: the Durrani Empire
formables.desc: Ahmad Shah Durrani founded Afghanistan and ruled from Mashhad to Delhi. Peshawar and the Punjab were Afghan before they were British.

formables.title: the Ghaznavid Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Khorasan and Hindustan

formables.desc: Mahmud of Ghazni raided India seventeen times from his mountain capital. His empire joined Khorasan to the Punjab.

formables.title: Assyria
formables.desc: Assyria ruled the Near East from Nineveh. The Assyrians of the Mosul plain and Urmia still speak the old language and want a homeland.

formables.title: the Babylonian Empire
formables.desc: Nebuchadnezzar made Babylon the wonder of the world and ruled from the Gulf to Jerusalem. Iraq can claim his legacy.

formables.title: the Akkadian Empire
formables.desc: Sargon of Akkad built the first empire in history, from the Persian Gulf to the Mediterranean. Its heartland is modern Iraq.

formables.title: the Levant
formables.desc: Syria, Lebanon, Palestine and Transjordan were one land under the Ottomans. Arab nationalists call it Greater Syria.

formables.title: Greater Israel
formables.desc: Revisionist Zionists claimed both banks of the Jordan for a Jewish state. In this world the Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem could become its seed.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Jerusalem
formables.desc: For eighty-eight years Crusader kings ruled from Jerusalem. The Knights of Malta still keep the memory of the Latin kingdom alive.

formables.title: Outremer

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Levant Coast

formables.desc: The four Crusader states of the Levant were called Outremer, "the land beyond the sea". A new crusade could restore them.

formables.title: Phoenicia
formables.desc: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos taught the world the alphabet and sailed to Spain. Lebanese Phoenicianists see them as the true ancestors of the nation.

formables.title: Carthage
formables.desc: "Carthago delenda est," said Cato, and Rome obeyed. But Carthage once ruled the western Mediterranean, and Tunis stands where it stood.

formables.title: the Umayyad Caliphate

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Arab World

formables.desc: Within a century of the Prophet, the Umayyads ruled from Damascus over an empire stretching from Spain to the Indus.

formables.title: the Abbasid Caliphate

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Arab World

formables.desc: From Baghdad, the City of Peace, the Abbasid caliphs presided over the golden age of Islam.

formables.title: the Mamluk Sultanate
formables.desc: The slave-soldiers who became sultans stopped the Mongols at Ain Jalut and ruled Egypt and Syria for two and a half centuries.

formables.title: the Ayyubid Sultanate

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Egypt and the Levant

formables.desc: Saladin, a Kurd from Tikrit, united Egypt and Syria and retook Jerusalem from the Crusaders. His dynasty ruled from Cairo to Yemen.

formables.title: the Bani Khalid Emirate
formables.desc: Before the House of Saud, the Bani Khalid ruled the oases of al-Hasa and the pearl coast of the Gulf.

formables.title: the Zaidi Kingdom of Yemen
formables.desc: The Zaidi imams have ruled the Yemeni highlands for a thousand years. With Hadhramaut and Dhofar, Yemen would be whole.

formables.title: Greater Egypt
formables.desc: Muhammad Ali Pasha made Egypt a great power, conquering Sudan, Syria and the Hejaz before the Europeans stopped him.

formables.title: the Middle East

names.social_liberal: Federal Republic of the Middle East
names.authoritarian_democrat: Federal State of the Middle East

formables.desc: From the Bosporus to the Gulf, the Middle East was one world under the caliphs and sultans. Make it one state again.

formables.title: North Africa
formables.desc: From the Atlantic to the Nile, North Africa shares a language, a faith and a coastline. One state could unite them all.

formables.title: the Sahel
formables.desc: The Sahel belt from the Niger to Darfur was home to Mali, Songhai and Kanem-Bornu. Its peoples share the desert edge and its hardships.

formables.title: Sub-Saharan Africa
formables.desc: South of the great desert lies most of Africa and almost all of its colonies. One state from Dakar to the Cape would end colonial rule for good.

formables.title: the Mali Empire
formables.desc: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca crashed the price of gold in Cairo. His empire ruled the western Sahel from Timbuktu to the Atlantic.

formables.title: the Kingdom of Aksum
formables.desc: Aksum was one of the great powers of the ancient world, ruling the Red Sea from Ethiopia to Yemen and minting its own gold.

formables.title: the Bantu Kingdom
formables.desc: From Cameroon to the Cape, the Bantu-speaking peoples share a common ancestry. Unite them in one great African state.

formables.title: the Mughal Empire
formables.desc: Akbar and Aurangzeb ruled a quarter of the world's people from Delhi and Agra. Restore the Peacock Throne.

formables.title: Akhand Bharat
formables.desc: Undivided India, from the Hindu Kush to Burma and from the Himalayas to Ceylon. Indian nationalists of every stripe have dreamed of it.

formables.title: the Pala Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Bengal and Bihar

formables.desc: The Buddhist Pala kings ruled Bengal and Bihar for four centuries and patronised the great university of Nalanda.

formables.title: the Bengal Sultanate
formables.desc: Bengal was the richest province of the Mughal Empire and, before that, an independent sultanate. United, the Bengalis would be a great nation.

formables.title: the Chola Empire
formables.desc: Rajendra Chola sent fleets across the Bay of Bengal and ruled from Ceylon to the Ganges. The Dravidian south can be a great power of its own.

formables.title: the Timurid Empire
formables.desc: Timur the Lame filled Samarkand with the wealth of half of Asia and made it the most beautiful city in the world. His heirs can do it again.

formables.title: the Chagatai Khanate
formables.desc: Chinggis Khan gave Central Asia to his son Chagatai. His khanate bridged Transoxiana and the Tarim basin for two centuries.

formables.title: the Turkic Khaganate

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Turkic Steppe

formables.desc: The Blue Turks of the sixth century ruled from Manchuria to the Black Sea, the first empire to bear the Turkic name.

formables.title: the Kyrgyz Khaganate
formables.desc: In 840 the Yenisei Kyrgyz destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate and ruled Mongolia. Khakassia and Tuva remember them.

formables.title: the Uyghur Khaganate
formables.desc: From Ordu-Baliq on the Orkhon the Uyghur khagans ruled the steppe and rescued the Tang dynasty. Their people now live in the Tarim basin.

formables.title: the Xiongnu

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Mongolic Steppe

formables.desc: Two centuries before Christ the Xiongnu united the tribes of the steppe and made Han China pay tribute. Mongolia can become that power again.

formables.title: the Ilkhanate

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Iran and Mesopotamia

formables.desc: Hulagu Khan sacked Baghdad in 1258 and founded the Ilkhanate, a Mongol state ruling Persia from Tabriz.

formables.title: the Yuan Dynasty

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of China and Mongolia

formables.desc: Kublai Khan conquered the Song and ruled all of China and Mongolia from Khanbaliq. A new Great Khan could sit on the Dragon Throne.

formables.title: the Liao Dynasty
formables.desc: The Khitan Liao ruled Manchuria, Mongolia and the lands around Beijing for two centuries. Their name gave the West the word "Cathay".

formables.title: the Qing Dynasty
formables.desc: The Qing emperors ruled the largest China in history, from Manchuria to Tibet. The Dragon Throne in Beijing is empty. Fill it.

formables.title: the Ming Dynasty
formables.desc: The Ming drove out the Mongols and restored Han rule over China. Secret societies still swear to "overthrow the Qing and restore the Ming".

formables.title: the Tang Dynasty
formables.desc: Under the Tang, Chang'an was the greatest city on earth and Chinese garrisons stood in the Tarim basin. A golden age can return.

formables.title: Greater Tibet
formables.desc: Songtsen Gampo's empire once threatened the Tang. Kham and Amdo are Tibetan lands held by Chinese warlords. Bring them home.

formables.title: the Himalayan Federation
formables.desc: Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan and Tibet share mountains, monasteries and a fear of their giant neighbours. A Himalayan union could defend them.

formables.title: Druk Yul
formables.desc: The Thunder Dragon kingdom lost the Duars to Britain in 1865. A stronger Bhutan could take back the lowlands and Sikkim.

formables.title: Greater Korea
formables.desc: Koreans have lived north of the Yalu since Goguryeo. Nationalists see Gando and southern Manchuria as Korean land.

formables.title: Unified Silla and Balhae
formables.desc: In the eighth century Silla ruled the peninsula and Balhae ruled Manchuria, both heirs of the Korean kingdoms. Unite the two.

formables.title: Goguryeo
formables.desc: Goguryeo held off Sui and Tang armies from its fortresses in Manchuria. Its kingdom spanned both banks of the Yalu.

formables.title: Greater Japan
formables.desc: Japan already rules Korea, Taiwan and southern Sakhalin. Add Manchuria and the German South Seas, and the empire will stretch from the Kurils to Micronesia.

formables.title: the Philippine Empire
formables.desc: Filipino nationalists claim Sabah, and some dream of a Malay maritime empire ruled from Manila.

formables.title: the Srivijaya Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of Sumatra and Malaya

formables.desc: From Palembang, Srivijaya controlled the Strait of Malacca and the trade between China and India for six centuries.

formables.title: the Khmer Empire
formables.desc: The kings of Angkor ruled most of mainland Southeast Asia. Siam and Vietnam have eaten away at Cambodia ever since. Reverse it.

formables.title: the Toungoo Empire
formables.desc: Bayinnaung of Toungoo built the largest empire in Southeast Asian history, ruling Siam, Laos and Manipur from Pegu.

formables.title: Southeast Asia
formables.desc: Burmese, Thai, Vietnamese, Malays and Filipinos have all lived under colonial rule or its threat. A Southeast Asian state would answer to no empire.

formables.title: Indochina
formables.desc: Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia were ruled together by France and now by Germany. Independent, they could stand together.

formables.title: Central America
formables.desc: From 1823 to 1841 the five Central American states were one federal republic. Morazán died trying to save it.

formables.title: the Mexican Empire
formables.desc: Agustín de Iturbide was crowned Emperor of Mexico in 1822, ruling from Central America to California. The gringos took half of it.

formables.title: the Viceroyalty of New Spain
formables.desc: For three centuries the Viceroy in Mexico City ruled from Panama to San Francisco, and even Manila. Reassemble New Spain.

formables.title: the Maya Empire

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Maya Lands

formables.desc: The Maya never had a single empire, but their cities shared one civilisation across Yucatán, Guatemala and Belize. The rebels of the Caste War still remember.

formables.title: the Caribbean
formables.desc: Betances and Martí dreamed of an Antillean Confederation of Cuba, Santo Domingo and Puerto Rico. Add Jamaica and the rest of the islands.

formables.title: Hispaniola
formables.desc: From 1822 to 1844 the whole island of Hispaniola was ruled from Port-au-Prince. Haitians and Dominicans could share it again.

formables.title: the Republic of Pirates
formables.desc: In 1706 the pirates of Nassau declared their own republic, with no king and an elected captain. The Caribbean can have free ports again.

formables.title: United Guyana
formables.desc: British, Dutch and French Guiana are three colonies on one coast. Independent, they would be stronger together.

formables.title: Greater Brazil
formables.desc: The Empire of Brazil once held Uruguay as its Cisplatine Province. Brazilian expansionists look to the Guianas and the River Plate.

formables.title: the Guaraní State
formables.desc: Guaraní is still the language of the Paraguayan people. The old Jesuit missions spanned Paraguay, Misiones and southern Brazil.

formables.title: the Muisca Confederation

names.social_democrat: Federal Republic of the Chibcha Lands

formables.desc: The Muisca of the Bogotá highlands were the fourth great civilisation of the Americas, and the source of the legend of El Dorado.

formables.title: the Andean Federation
formables.desc: The Andean republics share mountains, mines and the legacies of the Inca and of Bolívar. A federation from Caracas to Santiago would command the spine of South America.

formables.title: the Chilean-Argentine Union

names.social_conservative: United Provinces of the Southern Cone

formables.desc: Chile and Argentina share the longest border in the Americas and nearly went to war over it in 1902. A union would end the rivalry for good.

formables.title: Greater Canada
formables.desc: With Newfoundland and Alaska, the Dominion would span the whole top of the continent, from the Atlantic to the Bering Strait.

formables.title: the Greater United States
formables.desc: Manifest Destiny never stopped at the Rio Grande or the 49th parallel. Bring Canada, Cuba and Hawaii into one continental republic.

formables.title: the Anglosphere

names.syndicalist: Combined Syndicates of the English-Speaking World
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Commonwealth of the English-Speaking Peoples

formables.desc: The Imperial Federation League wanted one parliament for the whole British world. Add the Americans, and the English-speaking peoples would rule the seas.

formables.title: the Golden Circle

names.social_liberal: Federal Republic of the Gulf of Mexico
names.authoritarian_democrat: Federal State of the Gulf of Mexico

formables.desc: Before the Civil War the Knights of the Golden Circle plotted a slaveholding empire around the Gulf of Mexico. In the chaos of the new American civil war, their heirs have revived the scheme.

formables.title: Greater Australasia
formables.desc: In 1890 New Zealand nearly joined the Australian federation. A greater Australasia would add New Guinea and Fiji as well.

formables.title: Melanesia
formables.desc: From New Guinea to Fiji, the Melanesian islands share a culture of big men, gardens and the wantok. A Melanesian federation would give them a voice.

formables.title: Polynesia
formables.desc: In 1887 King Kalākaua of Hawaii proposed a Polynesian Confederation with Samoa. From Hawaii to Easter Island and Aotearoa, the Polynesian triangle could be one nation.

formables.title: the Pacific Union
formables.desc: Thousands of islands scattered across the largest ocean on earth. Unite Micronesia, Melanesia and Polynesia into one Pacific state.

formables.title: Oceania
formables.desc: Australia, New Zealand and the islands of the South Pacific: a continent made mostly of ocean, under a single government.

formables.title: the Asian Union
formables.desc: Pan-Asianists from Tokyo to Calcutta dreamed of an Asia for the Asians. Unite the largest continent under one government.

formables.title: Eurasia
formables.desc: From Lisbon to Tokyo the supercontinent is a single landmass. Hold its great capitals and make it a single state.

formables.title: Afro-Eurasia

names.radical_socialist: Socialist Union of the Old World
names.social_democrat: United States of the Old World
names.authoritarian_democrat: Federal State of the Old World

formables.desc: Three continents joined by land: the Old World of every ancient empire. Rule all of it.

formables.title: the Americas
formables.desc: Bolívar dreamed of uniting the Americas at the Congress of Panama. From Alaska to Patagonia: one hemisphere, one state.

formables.title: Hispanic America

names.totalist: Union of Latin American Socialist Republics

formables.desc: From the Rio Grande to Tierra del Fuego, eighteen republics speak one language. Bolívar and San Martín meant them to be one nation.

formables.title: a World Government

names.syndicalist: Socialist Workers Union of the World

formables.desc: Every empire in history wanted the whole world. Hold the ten great capitals and make your flag the only one left.
